messages:
kelly: :rotating_light: alex-cust reporting sudden p99 spike (~9-12s) on /v1/generate starting ~2025-03-03 09:12 UTC after our last canary. Customer says it impacts 10% of requests, mostly larger prompts. They shared a request id and a repro curl.
raj: Can you paste tenant id, model, region, and an example request (no customer PII)? Also any recent deploy info?
kelly: tenant: tenant_837, model: redwood-v2-small, region: us-west-2. Canary rolled ~09:05 UTC. Example repro curl below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-small","input":"<~500 token prompt>","max_tokens":256}'
```
kelly: Customer-provided request id: req_20250303_091234. They see p95 ~300ms but p99 ~9-12s.
deploy-bot: Canary redwood-v2-small @us-west-2 completed at 2025-03-03T09:05:12Z; rollout to 10% traffic.
raj: grabbing metrics — can you hold for 2-3 min? Share traces if available.
raj: metrics snapshot: admit_queue_depth by shard: [shard-3: 420, shard-7: 310], worker_cpu: shard-3 host-12 98%, gpu_util: 95% on host-12, worker_restarts host-12 x2 in last 10m, kv_cache_miss_rate increased from 2% -> 18% during spike.
ana: (typo should be ana) ana: seeing a hot host (host-12) with repeated CUDA OOM events and long model load times -> worker falling behind, causing admission queue buildup. Likely cascade: slow loads -> KV cache cold -> larger batches queued -> tail latency.
raj: probable cause: overload on a subset of workers after canary (maybe different memory / quant config). Immediate mitigations to try:
  - move traffic away from shard-3 (reroute) or drain host-12
  - temporarily increase pool size (+2 replicas) for redwood-v2-small in us-west-2
  - lower admission threshold (allow less queuing) and enable burst capacity for enterprise tenants
ana: can also switch this tenant to a warm-start / preloaded variant (redwood-v2-small-warm) or fallback to quantized variant redwood-v2-small-8q if acceptable for quality.
kelly: applying ramp: 1) draining host-12, 2) +2 replicas in pool (scaling up), 3) lowered per-worker max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for redwood-v2-small in us-west-2. Will monitor.
raj: noted. Also add a short-lived priority lane for tiered customers so their requests bypass regular admission queue (only for tenant_837) — will coordinate with infra.
kelly: applied scale-up and batch size change at 09:22 UTC. Observed p95 drop to ~350ms, p99 improved to ~3.1s but still above SLO. admit_queue_depth on shard-3 dropped to ~70.
ana: good improvement — next step: either rollback canary or route tenant_837 to a warmed variant. Which do we prefer? Rolling back will remove new bug risk but slow traffic change can be disruptive.
kelly: customer prefers fastest fix -> will switch their traffic to redwood-v2-small-8q (quant) for now, update them that quality diff is minimal for their prompts.
raj: doing temporary priority reroute + update service routing (tenant_837 -> redwood-v2-small-8q, us-west-2). Also flagged host-12 for postmortem.
kelly: updated customer at 09:31 UTC, they confirm p99 reduced to ~450ms on their samples. :white_check_mark:
ana: action items:
  - ana -> eng-runtime to root cause drift between canary and default (config, memory/quant differences) (owner: ana)
  - raj -> infra to investigate host-12 OOMs and autoscaling/placement heuristics (owner: raj)
  - kelly -> support to continue customer updates and validate no regressions for 24h (owner: kelly)
  - infra -> consider automating warm variants for heavy prompt profiles (owner: infra)
kelly: creating follow-up ticket DEV-PLAT-5234 with logs + traces + request ids. Will attach heap logs from host-12 and sample traces.
alex-cust: thanks team — we can tolerate small quality diff for now, appreciate the quick fix.
kelly: marking thread stable for now. If p99 creeps back up we'll reopen and consider canary rollback. Closing in 30m if metrics stay stable.
